# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Puzzles

## Primary Classification by Core Mechanic

---

## 1. NUMBER PLACEMENT PUZZLES
*Place or fill numbers into cells according to constraints*

### 1.1 Latin Square / Uniqueness Constraints
- **Sudoku** — Fill 1–9 in rows, columns, and 3×3 blocks
- **Hitori** — Eliminate duplicates in rows/columns by blacking cells

### 1.2 Region-Based Number Filling
- **Fillomino** — Fill blocks where each cell's number equals block size
- **Ripple Effect** — Fill rooms with 1–N; duplicates must be separated by ≥ that value
- **Makaro** — Fill rooms with 1–N; arrows indicate which neighbor cell holds the maximum

### 1.3 Number Placement with External Clues
- **Kurodoko** — Numbers indicate total visible white cells in cross directions
- **Kurotto** — Numbers indicate sum of adjacent black cell groups
- **Nansuke** — Fill a crossword-style grid with numbers from a provided list

---

## 2. REGION DIVISION PUZZLES
*Divide the grid into regions according to rules*

### 2.1 Rectangular / Rectilinear Division
- **Shikaku** — Divide into rectangles, each containing exactly one number equal to its area
- **Choco Banana** — Divide into rectangles/squares (black) and non-rectangular regions (white) with size clues

### 2.2 Polyomino Division
- **Five Cells** — Divide grid into pentominoes; numbers indicate boundary line count
- **LITS** — Shade one tetromino per region; same-shape tetrominoes cannot touch

### 2.3 Paired / Symmetric Division
- **Double Choco** — Divide into blocks each containing a white and gray area of identical shape
- **Nuritwin** — Each region contains two same-sized shaded blocks

### 2.4 Shaped Block Division
- **Sashigane** — Divide into L-shaped blocks; circles mark bends, arrows mark ends
- **Evolomino** — Divide into blocks that grow sequentially along arrow paths

---

## 3. CELL SHADING / PAINTING PUZZLES
*Determine which cells to color black (or shade)*

### 3.1 Connectivity and Isolation Constraints
- **Nurikabe** — Shade cells to form a connected wall; white islands match given numbers
- **Heyawake** — Shade cells by room counts; no two shaded cells touch; white cells stay connected
- **Usowan** — Shade cells with neighbor counts, but one number per bold region is deliberately wrong

### 3.2 Shape-Constrained Shading
- **Chained Block** — Black cells form blocks; blocks in a chain must all differ in size/shape
- **Norinori** — Shade cells in dominoes; each bold region contains exactly two shaded cells
- **Sto-stone** — Shade cells in rooms; when "dropped," shaded cells fill exactly the bottom half

### 3.3 Shading with Geometric White-Space Rules
- **Shakashaka** — Place right triangles in cells so remaining white space forms rectangles
- **Choco Banana** — Black groups must be rectangular; white groups must not be rectangular

### 3.4 Shading with Visibility / Directional Clues
- **Tilepaint** — Color whole tiles; diagonal clue cells indicate count of black cells in row/column segments
- **Nurimeizu** — Shade rooms to create a maze from S to G; circles lie on shortest path, triangles do not

### 3.5 Promontory / Connectivity Shading
- **Nurimisaki** — Circle cells are promontories (one white neighbor); numbers indicate white line length

---

## 4. LOOP DRAWING PUZZLES
*Draw a single closed loop through the grid*

### 4.1 Unconstrained Path with Cell Markers
- **Slitherlink** — Loop along grid edges; numbers indicate how many sides of that cell are used
- **Masyu** — Loop through all circles; black = turn then straight, white = straight then turn
- **Mid-loop** — Loop through all black circles, which must be the midpoint of a straight segment

### 4.2 Region / Room Traversal Loops
- **Moon-or-Sun** — Loop visits each room once; alternates between visiting all moons or all suns
- **Dotchi-Loop** — Loop through white circles; per bold region, all circles are either turns or straights
- **Suraromu** — Loop passes through numbered gates in a specified order

### 4.3 Directional / Wind-Constrained Loops
- **Nagareru** — Loop direction set by arrow cells; wind from black cells forbids movement against it
- **Yajilin** — Loop avoids black cells; arrow clues give count of black cells in that direction

---

## 5. PATH AND CONNECTION PUZZLES
*Connect elements or trace paths through the grid*

### 5.1 Island Connection
- **Hashiwokakero** — Connect numbered islands with bridges (1–2 per pair); all islands linked

### 5.2 Pair Connection
- **Numberlink** — Connect matching number pairs with non-crossing, non-branching lines

### 5.3 Sequential Path Placement
- **Hebi** — Place snakes (sequences 1–5) in white cells; snakes cannot touch or "see" each other

---

## 6. OBJECT PLACEMENT PUZZLES
*Place discrete objects into the grid according to constraints*

### 6.1 Light / Visibility Placement
- **Akari** — Place light bulbs so every white cell is lit; numbered cells indicate adjacent bulb count

### 6.2 Symbol / Mark Placement
- **Juosan** — Fill cells with — or |; territory clues give the difference in counts; marks cannot extend too far in their perpendicular direction

### 6.3 Block / Piece Placement
- **Evolomino** — Place growing square blocks along arrow routes *(also see Region Division)*

### 6.4 Pencil / Segment Placement
- **Pencils** — Identify pencil bodies and draw lines from tips; line length matches number in pencil

---

## 7. MOVEMENT / MIGRATION PUZZLES
*Move or relocate existing grid elements*

### 7.1 Circle Migration
- **Satogaeri** — Move circles into their home regions; number indicates distance traveled
- **Yosenabe** — Move numbered circles into gray areas; gray area total must match sum of entering circles

---

## Summary Table

| Category | Subcategory | Puzzles |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Number Placement** | Latin Square | Sudoku, Hitori |
| | Region Filling | Fillomino, Ripple Effect, Makaro |
| | External Clues | Kurodoko, Kurotto, Nansuke |
| **2. Region Division** | Rectangular | Shikaku, Choco Banana |
| | Polyomino | Five Cells, LITS |
| | Paired/Symmetric | Double Choco, Nuritwin |
| | Shaped Block | Sashigane, Evolomino |
| **3. Cell Shading** | Connectivity | Nurikabe, Heyawake, Usowan |
| | Shape-Constrained | Chained Block, Norinori, Sto-stone |
| | Geometric White-Space | Shakashaka, Choco Banana |
| | Directional Clues | Tilepaint, Nurimeizu |
| | Promontory | Nurimisaki |
| **4. Loop Drawing** | Cell Markers | Slitherlink, Masyu, Mid-loop |
| | Room Traversal | Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Suraromu |
| | Directional | Nagareru, Yajilin |
| **5. Path & Connection** | Island Connection | Hashiwokakero |
| | Pair Connection | Numberlink |
| | Sequential Path | Hebi |
| **6. Object Placement** | Light/Visibility | Akari |
| | Symbol/Mark | Juosan |
| | Pencil/Segment | Pencils |
| **7. Movement / Migration** | Circle Migration | Satogaeri, Yosenabe |

---

> **Note on multi-category puzzles:** Several puzzles combine mechanics from more than one category. *Choco Banana* involves both region division and shading rules. *Evolomino* involves both region division and sequential placement. *Yajilin* combines loop drawing with cell shading. These puzzles are placed in their **dominant** mechanic category with cross-references where appropriate.
